## What the marts show (descriptive)

Charts are rendered by [`scripts/build_insights.py`](../scripts/build_insights.py) from the tested marts on each build. Sales comparisons use the {comp_stores} comparable stores open all {weeks} weeks without a remodel.

![Weekly net sales, comparable stores, FY2024 vs FY2025](assets/insights/weekly_net_sales.svg)

Comparable-store sales grew **{comp_growth}** — well below the {chain_growth} chain total, which is inflated by the store that opened in FY2025.

![Net sales and gross margin by subcategory](assets/insights/subcategory_performance.svg)

Like-for-like, {shrinking} of {n_subcats} subcategories shrank. {growers} grew; **{margin_loser}** changed sales by {margin_loser_sales} and margin by {margin_loser_pp}; {largest}, the largest subcategory, changed {largest_sales} and {largest_pp}. Margins are before vendor funding; these are descriptive changes, not causal effects.

![Forecast accuracy by fiscal period](assets/insights/forecast_accuracy.svg)

The forecast **over-forecasts in {fc_periods}** (FY2025 bias {fc_bias_fy25}, WAPE {fc_wape_fy25}), using two-week-lead forecasts only; actuals may be stock-constrained.

![Estimated vendor funding owed but not billed](assets/insights/funding_gap_by_vendor.svg)

The upper bound of the funding gap, by vendor: it assumes every approved event and planned display ran. Scan-back on observed units alone accounts for {v_low} of the {v_high}. ## The five business questions

The [decision memo](decision_memo.md) answers each question with a dollar figure, a 90% range and a recommendation, or says plainly when the data cannot answer. The methods are explained without jargon in [methods in plain English](methods_explained.md).

| Question | What the evidence supports | Recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| Delist slow sellers? | **Inconclusive.** With four test stores the test cannot detect a gross-profit change under {d_mde}, and the same comparison on a fake date a year earlier shows a {d_fake24} "effect", so large-store seasonality confounds it. What it did measure cleanly: units fell {d_units} but net sales changed only {d_sales}, because shoppers switched to the items that stayed (retained items recovered {d_transfer} of the lost sales, {d_transfer_ci}). | Don't roll out the test planogram. Treat the {a_cuts} SKUs that earn the least gross profit per facing as candidates ({a_value} if the transfer rate holds) and pilot their removal with a store holdout, large-format stores first: the rate was measured in four large stores only |
| Promotions | **Roughly break-even, and only because of vendor money.** FY2025 events net {q2_net} ({q2_ci}) after funding and {q2_before} before it; {q2_pos_before} of events made money on their own. | Drop promotions without a display; keep display events where execution is verified and the fee collected |
| Spring 2025 price increases | **Not identified** by either event design. *Validated:* the break-even elasticities ({p_gr_be} for Golden Ridge, {p_bs_be} for tortilla) are arithmetic on price and cost. *Scenario:* an unvalidated pooled elasticity ({p_gr_pooled} for kettle, {p_bs_pooled} for private-label tortilla) puts Golden Ridge far from break-even and tortilla near it. | Keep Golden Ridge's price, assuming the pooled estimate is roughly right; tortilla: {e_tortilla_action}, a scenario call on small dollars |
| Forecast and in-stock | Over-forecasts by {f_bias} ({f_bias_ci}) while beating naive benchmarks; a correction learned on FY2024 cut FY2025 bias to {f_bias_after} out of sample. {ph_readme} Stock-outs cost an estimated {o_gp} of GP ({o_ci}, exploratory). | Use the corrected forecast for budgets; leave store replenishment alone |
| Vendor funding | Approved events were under-billed by {v_low} to {v_high}. The low end is scan-back on observed units; the high end also counts display fees for every planned display, which the extracts cannot confirm ran. | Bill the {v_low} scan-back shortfall now; verify displays before billing the display portion |

### The FY2026 plan

{plan_readme}

**How the analysis is checked.** Estimators recover planted effects in simulated and real data; every headline coefficient and clustered standard error is re-estimated by an independent pure-Python solver and by R `fixest` in CI; CI fails if the memo, the plan, this page or any result drifts from what the queries produce. {scorecard_readme}

**What the analysis plan does and doesn't prove.** The [analysis plan](../analysis/PLAN.md) set the metrics, comparison groups and decision rules before the first results commit, and later changes are logged as deviations. It is not a formal pre-registration; [methods in plain English](methods_explained.md#the-fixed-analysis-plan-and-what-it-does-and-doesnt-prove) explains the timing and the history rewrite.
